samples.summary: The human summary mixes the FULL total with EMITTED-only counts, so the non-blocking/demoted split and both tally tables are wrong whenever the record is trimmed
samples.evidence: `buildDeferredCheck` (line 362) calls `renderDeferredSummary({ total, emitted, omitted, records: records.slice(0, emitted), ... })` — `total` counts every deferred finding, but `records` is only the surviving prefix. Inside `renderDeferredSummary`, `const demoted = rows.filter((r) => r?.lane === "backlog").length` (line 296) counts only the emitted rows, and line 300 then prints `${total} finding(s) ... ${total - demoted} non-blocking, ${demoted} demoted`. With total=60 and emitted=10 (3 of them demoted), the body claims "60 findings: 57 non-blocking, 3 demoted" even though the real demoted count over all 60 is unknown/larger — the two populations the docblock insists must stay distinguishable are silently mis-split. The same defect affects the `| lens | n |` and `| severity | n |` tables (lines 302-308): they are computed from `rows` (emitted) but sit under a headline stating `total`, so their column sums do not equal the stated total and a reader attributes the deficit to nothing. Note the existing tests only exercise the split on an untrimmed set (`the summary splits the two populations`, deferred-findings.test.mjs:281), so nothing catches this. Fix: pass the full `records` for tallying, or derive/pass a demoted count over all records.

samples.summary: `if: always()` posts a "None this round" deferred record for panels that were CANCELLED or never produced verdicts, the exact empty-record lie the module's main() claims to refuse
samples.evidence: Both new steps use `if: always() && steps.pr.outputs.number != ''` (lines 1089 and 1114). The sibling step that writes the per-lens check runs deliberately uses `!cancelled()` (line 927) with a long comment explaining that a cancelled panel is a SUPERSEDED one and that writing check runs for it put phantom results on the commit (#695). Under `always()`, a cancelled/superseded or crashed panel leaves `.agent-review/<lens>/verdict.json` absent, `readLensFindings` (deferred-findings.mjs:376) skips every missing directory and returns `[]`, and `buildDeferredCheck` happily emits `total: 0` with `renderDeferredSummary`'s `"None this round."` (line 278). That is precisely the outcome `main()` refuses in the manifest case — "refuse rather than write an empty record that reads as 'this round deferred nothing'" (deferred-findings.mjs:410-412) — but the review-dir case has no such guard: nothing distinguishes "the round deferred nothing" from "the round never ran". An archive whose whole value is comparability across rounds is then seeded with false zero rows.

samples.summary: The PARTIAL notice hard-codes MAX_TEXT_CHARS instead of the budget actually applied, so it states a wrong number whenever a custom `maxChars` is used
samples.evidence: `buildDeferredCheck` accepts `maxChars = MAX_TEXT_CHARS` (line 351) and forwards it to `buildDeferredText`, but `renderDeferredSummary` is never told the budget and prints `` `${omitted} were dropped to fit the ${MAX_TEXT_CHARS} character budget.` `` (line 313-314). Called with `maxChars: 4000` (as deferred-findings.test.mjs:293 does) the body claims findings were dropped to fit 60000 characters while 4000 was enforced. Harmless on the production path today only because the workflow never passes `maxChars`.

samples.summary: The deferred check is always `checks.create`d, so a re-run of the panel on the same head SHA leaves two contradictory `agent-deferred-findings` runs
samples.evidence: Line 1130 unconditionally calls `github.rest.checks.create({ name: check.name, head_sha: context.payload.workflow_run.head_sha, ... })`. The lens checks immediately above solve the same problem by preferring `checks.update` on the in-progress run (lines 1043-1059, "one run per lens transitions in_progress → completed, so the PR shows ... never a duplicate"). The panel is explicitly re-runnable on the same head sha (`github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt > 1` is an accepted trigger, line 160), so attempt 2 stacks a second neutral record — and if attempt 2 is the cancelled/empty one, the PR shows both "40 deferred" and "0 deferred" for the same commit with no way to tell which is current.

samples.summary: `isDeferred` short-circuits on severity before testing the lane, so a non-blocking finding carrying `lane: "discarded"` would be filed as deferred work — the population the docblock says must never appear
samples.evidence: `if (!BLOCKING.has(normalizeSeverity(finding.severity))) return true;` (line 137) returns before the `lane === "backlog"` test on line 138, so `{ severity: "minor", lane: "discarded" }` is deferred while `{ severity: "major", lane: "discarded" }` is not. The docblock (lines 116-123) and the test at deferred-findings.test.mjs:69 only assert the blocking case. Today `annotateFindings` returns non-blockers untouched (review-panel.mjs:842) so no non-blocker can carry a lane, which is why this is latent rather than live — but the guard is asymmetric in exactly the direction the module says would "poison the pile with claims the panel already decided were wrong". An explicit `finding.lane === "discarded" → false` first would make the rule independent of that upstream invariant.

samples.summary: Findings from a lens whose `gating` is not `blocking` are not captured, although they are by definition findings the gate did not act on
samples.evidence: `isDeferred` classifies purely on severity and `lane`. For an ADVISORY lens the panel forces a success conclusion regardless of severity (see `advisory` handling in `writeVerdict`/`renderSummaryMd`, review-panel.mjs:3446-3453 and severity.mjs:313-321), so its critical/major findings carry `lane: "blocking"` yet gate nothing — and `collectDeferred` therefore excludes exactly the findings the channel exists to record. `scripts/agent/lenses/lenses.json` currently declares all six lenses `"gating": "blocking"`, so this is latent, but the manifest is data and the module reads it without consulting the field.

verdict.reason: Code is exactly as described. buildDeferredCheck (deferred-findings.mjs:362) passes the full `total` (computed over all records, line 253/353) together with `records: records.slice(0, emitted)`. renderDeferredSummary then derives `demoted` from those emitted rows only (line 296) and prints `${total - demoted} non-blocking, ${demoted} demoted` (line 300), mixing populations; tally() (284-291) likewise counts only emitted rows while its tables sit under the `total` headline (302-308), so column sums do not equal the stated total. Trimming is reachable: buildDeferredText drops trailing records to fit MAX_TEXT_CHARS (258-263) with per-record fields clipped at 2000 chars each (180-181), and the existing test at deferred-findings.test.mjs:272-276 demonstrates trimming firing. The PARTIAL notice (311-317) flags partiality but does not fix the split or tables. Tests only cover the split on an untrimmed set (test.mjs:280-288), so nothing catches it. Real logic/reporting bug in the Correctness lane; no guard elsewhere prevents it.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. Both new deferred-findings steps use `if: always() && steps.pr.outputs.number != ''` (agent-review-panel.yml:1089, 1114), while the sibling per-lens check-run writer deliberately uses `!cancelled()` (:927) with a comment documenting that under `always()` the step DID run on a cancelled/superseded panel, saw no panel.json, and wrote phantom results that `fixAttemptCommits` mis-counted (#695) — i.e. the repo itself establishes that these always() steps execute on cancelled runs with an absent/partial .agent-review tree. On that path `readLensFindings` (deferred-findings.mjs:378-393) skips every missing verdict.json and returns [], and `buildDeferredCheck` (:351-368) emits `total: 0` with `renderDeferredSummary`'s "None this round." (:274-283). `main()` (:406-415) guards only the unreadable-manifest case with the explicit rationale "refuse rather than write an empty record that reads as 'this round deferred nothing'"; there is no equivalent review-dir/verdict-presence guard, so a superseded or crashed round is recorded identically to a round that genuinely deferred nothing. No guard elsewhere blocks it: `continue-on-error` only suppresses redness, the `[ -f .trusted/...deferred-findings.mjs ]` check (:1094) passes since .trusted is checked out early, `steps.pr.outputs.number` is set well before a mid-panel cancellation, and `assertAdvisory` (:335-348) only checks name/conclusion. Advisory status (neutral conclusion, name outside the `agent-review-` prefix set-state.mjs reads; grep finds no non-test consumer) limits blast radius but does not make the false-zero write correct — it is a mis-handled failure path violating the module's own stated invariant, which is in this lens.
